subject: Chemistry
title: Why Garlic Lingers on Your Breath
description: Learn Why Garlic Lingers on Your Breath in one minute.

hook.text: Garlic breath can last up to 72 hours because the smelly compounds enter your bloodstream and leave through your lungs.

buildup.text: Crushing garlic activates alliinase enzyme, which converts alliin into allicin—the sharp, pungent compound.

discovery.text: Allicin quickly breaks down into allyl methyl sulfide (AMS), which the body can't metabolize efficiently.

twist.text: AMS enters the blood, travels to the lungs, and is exhaled. Brushing your teeth doesn't help—it's coming from inside.

climax.text: Eating raw apple or drinking milk reduces garlic breath. The enzymes and fats bind AMS before it reaches the blood.

punchline.text: A sulfur compound your body can't break down. It leaves through your lungs.

quiz.question: Why can't brushing teeth eliminate garlic breath?
options: The odor compound enters the bloodstream and is exhaled from the lungs
Garlic oils permanently stain tooth enamel
Garlic bacteria survive in the stomach for days

details.summary: When garlic is crushed, the enzyme alliinase converts alliin to allicin, which rapidly breaks down into sulfur compounds including allyl methyl sulfide. This particular compound is absorbed into the bloodstream and exhaled through the lungs for up to 24 hours after consumption.
details.whyItMatters: Allicin and its derivatives are potent antimicrobials being studied for medical applications. Understanding garlic's sulfur chemistry has implications for food science, medicine, and agriculture.
takeaways: Crushing garlic activates alliinase enzyme to produce pungent allicin
Allyl methyl sulfide enters the bloodstream and escapes via the lungs
Breath odor persists because the compound bypasses normal digestion

faq.question: Why does chewing parsley help reduce garlic breath?
faq.answer: Parsley contains polyphenolic compounds and chlorophyll that react with sulfur compounds in the mouth, trapping or neutralizing them. Enzymatic deodorization by polyphenol oxidase also breaks down some volatile sulfur molecules. However, it cannot eliminate sulfides already in the bloodstream.

faq.question: Why does garlic only become pungent when cut or crushed?
faq.answer: Intact garlic cells keep alliin and the enzyme alliinase in separate compartments. Cutting or crushing ruptures cell walls, allowing the enzyme to contact alliin and rapidly convert it to allicin. This defense mechanism evolved to deter herbivores from eating the plant.
